title: Number Bonds to 10 and 20 (KS1)
subject: Maths
strapline: The pairs of numbers that add together to make 10 and 20.
facts: A number bond is a pair of numbers that add together to make a total.
Number bonds to 10: 0+10, 1+9, 2+8, 3+7, 4+6, 5+5 (and the same the other way round).
If you know 3+7=10, you also know 7+3=10 and 10−3=7 and 10−7=3 — that is a fact family.
Number bonds to 20 build on the ones to 10: 13+7=20 because 3+7=10.
Knowing bonds to 10 by heart makes adding bigger numbers much faster.
Ten frames and fingers are good ways to picture a bond.
teacher_tips: Rehearse to instant recall — bonds should be automatic, not counted each time.
Use a ten frame so children see the "gap to ten" as a picture.
Practise the whole fact family together, not each fact in isolation.
